easy.def: Being steady and not likely to fall or change.
examples: The table has stability.
Stability matters.
A boat needs stability.

more.def: The quality of being steady and firm, and not likely to fall, change or break down.
examples: The wide base of the lamp gives it stability.
The family wanted stability, so they stayed in one town.
A boat needs stability to stay upright in the waves.

easy.def: A building where horses are kept.
examples: The horse is in the stable.
The stable is clean.
She cleaned the stable.

more.def: A building where horses are kept and cared for.
examples: The horse trotted back to the stable.
She cleaned the stable each morning.
The stable smelled of hay.

easy.def: Steady and not likely to fall.
examples: The ladder is stable.
The table is stable.
The chair is stable.

more.def: Firm and steady, not likely to move or change.
examples: The ladder is stable on flat ground.
The table is stable, so it will not wobble.
The bridge is stable enough to hold a heavy truck.

easy.def: A neat pile of things.
examples: A stack of books is on the desk.
I made a stack of cards.
The stack of plates is tall.

more.def: A pile of things placed one on top of another.
examples: A stack of books sat on the desk.
She made a tall stack of blocks.
The stack of plates wobbled.

easy.def: To put things in a pile.
examples: Stack the cups.
She stacked the books.
He stacked the wood.

more.def: To place things on top of each other in a neat pile.
examples: Stack the plates by the sink.
He stacked the wood by the fire.
The kids stacked their toy blocks into a tower.

easy.def: A big place for sports games.
examples: We watched the game in the stadium.
The stadium is big.
The stadium is full.

more.def: A large outdoor building with seats around a field where sports are played.
examples: We watched the game at the stadium.
The stadium holds thousands of fans.
The crowd roared inside the stadium.

easy.def: The people who work at a place.
examples: The school staff are kind.
The hospital staff.
The staff helped us.

more.def: All the people who work in a place such as a school or store.
examples: The school staff greeted us at the door.
The hospital staff worked all night.
The restaurant staff wore aprons.

easy.def: A long stick.
examples: The shepherd had a staff.
The wizard held a staff.
He leaned on a staff.

more.def: A long stick used for walking or for show.
examples: The shepherd leaned on his staff.
The wizard held a glowing staff.
She carried a wooden staff on the hike.

easy.def: A raised floor where people perform.
examples: The singer walked on the stage.
The band is on the stage.
We climbed onto the stage.

more.def: A raised floor in a theater where actors and musicians perform.
examples: The actors bowed on the stage.
The band set up on the stage.
She walked across the stage to get her award.

easy.def: One step in a process.
examples: The first stage is easy.
A frog has a tadpole stage.
We finished the second stage.

more.def: One step or period in a process or in growing.
examples: A tadpole is one stage in a frog's life.
We finished the first stage of the project.
The plant is in an early stage of growth.

easy.def: A spot that is hard to wash off.
examples: There is a stain on my shirt.
The juice made a stain.
The stain will not come out.

more.def: A mark made by something that has soaked into cloth or other material.
examples: There is a grape juice stain on my shirt.
The red wine left a stain on the rug.
A coffee stain spread across the paper.

easy.def: To leave a spot on something.
examples: The juice will stain my shirt.
The berries stained my fingers.
The ink stained the table.

more.def: To leave a mark that is hard to get out.
examples: Berries stained my fingers purple.
The paint stained my jeans.
The tea stained the tablecloth.

easy.def: A set of steps going up or down.
examples: The staircase is long.
We climbed the staircase.
A staircase in the hall.

more.def: A set of stairs with the rails or walls around them that lead from one floor to another.
examples: We climbed the long staircase to the top floor.
A wooden staircase curved up to the attic.
The cat slept on the bottom of the staircase.

easy.def: Steps that go from one floor to another.
examples: I walk up the stairs.
The stairs are steep.
The cat ran down the stairs.

more.def: A set of steps that you walk up or down to go from one floor to another.
examples: We climbed the stairs to the top floor.
Be careful on the wet stairs.
The stairs creak when you step on them.

easy.def: The space in a building that has the stairs.
examples: We ran up the stairwell.
The stairwell was dark.
The stairwell echoes.

more.def: The part of a building that holds the stairs, usually with walls around it.
examples: Our voices echoed in the narrow stairwell of the old building.
The stairwell was lit by a single small window.
We climbed all ten floors by the stairwell.

easy.def: A pointed stick that you push into the ground.
examples: He hammered a stake into the ground.
The tent is tied to a stake.
A stake held up the plant.

more.def: A strong, pointed stick or post pushed into the ground to hold something up or in place.
examples: We tied the tent rope to a stake.
The gardener used a stake to hold up the tall flower.
He hammered a stake into the ground to mark the spot.

easy.def: Not fresh any more.
examples: The bread is stale.
I do not like stale crackers.
The air in the room was stale.

more.def: No longer fresh, such as food that has gone dry and hard, or air that has been shut in for a long time.
examples: The bread was stale and hard, so we gave it to the ducks.
The room smelled stale after being closed all summer.
Stale crackers lose their crunch and taste flat.

easy.def: The main stem of a plant.
examples: The corn has a stalk.
The flower stalk is long.
The stalk is green.

more.def: The long, thin main stem of a plant.
examples: The corn stalk grew tall.
The flower had a long green stalk.
The bean plant climbed up a stalk.

easy.def: A small stand where things are sold.
examples: The fruit stall is busy.
We bought a hat at the stall.
The stall sells flowers.

more.def: A small open booth or table where things are sold.
examples: We bought apples at the market stall.
The flower stall was full of roses.
A stall sold hot cocoa on the corner.

easy.def: A space in a barn for one animal.
examples: The horse is in its stall.
The cow has a stall.
The stall is clean.

more.def: A small space in a barn or stable for one animal.
examples: The horse stood quietly in its stall.
Each cow has a stall in the barn.
She cleaned out the stall.

easy.def: A grown-up male horse.
examples: The stallion ran fast.
A stallion is a male horse.
The stallion has a long mane.

more.def: An adult male horse, especially one used for breeding.
examples: The stallion galloped across the field.
A stallion is a grown male horse.
The black stallion shook its long mane in the wind.

easy.def: A small piece of paper you stick on a letter.
examples: I put a stamp on the letter.
The stamp has a picture.
I collect stamps.

more.def: A small label that you put on a letter or package to show that you paid to send it.
examples: I put a stamp on the envelope.
She collects stamps from other countries.
The stamp had a picture of a bird.

easy.def: To bring your foot down hard.
examples: I stamp my foot.
The child stamped.
He stamped on the floor.

more.def: To put your foot down hard and loudly.
examples: She stamped her foot in anger.
The horse stamped in the stall.
He stamped the snow off his boots.

easy.def: The way you stand.
examples: He took a stance.
Her stance was wide.
A good stance.

more.def: The way that you stand, especially when you are ready to do something, or the opinion that you take on a subject.
examples: The batter took a wide stance at the plate.
She took a strong stance against littering in the park.
A good stance helps you keep your balance.

easy.def: To be up on your legs.
examples: Stand up, please.
I stand in line.
The tree stood tall.

more.def: To be upright on your feet, or to be placed upright.
examples: Please stand when the flag goes by.
The old barn stood at the top of the hill.
Flamingos can stand on one leg for a long time.

easy.def: How good something has to be.
examples: The school has high standards.
This meets the standard.
Her work is above standard.

more.def: A level of quality that people expect something to reach.
examples: The restaurant has a high standard of cleanliness.
The cook did not meet the standard for the contest.
The school has high standards for good behavior.

easy.def: Usual and normal.
examples: A standard pencil is yellow.
The standard size is small.
This is the standard way to do it.

more.def: Normal and regular, and used by most people.
examples: A standard school bus is bright yellow.
The standard size for the paper is eight by eleven inches.
Pens come in the standard colors of black, blue and red.

easy.def: Someone or something ready to help if needed.
examples: The nurse is on standby.
A spare tire is a good standby.
We kept a standby ready.

more.def: A person or thing that is kept ready to be used if needed, or a state of being ready and waiting.
examples: The lifeguard stayed on standby near the edge of the pool.
A flashlight is a handy standby when the power goes out.
The singer was a standby in case the first one got sick.

easy.def: A small piece of metal that holds papers together.
examples: I put a staple in the paper.
The staple is bent.
A box of staples.

more.def: A small, thin piece of bent metal that is pushed through papers to hold them together, or a basic food that people eat often.
examples: The teacher put a staple in the top corner of the pages.
Rice is a staple food in many countries.
Bread and milk are staples in our kitchen.

easy.def: To join papers with a small piece of metal.
examples: Staple the papers.
I stapled the pages.
She stapled the note.

more.def: To join papers together with small pieces of bent metal.
examples: I stapled the pages of my report together.
She stapled the note to the door.
Please staple your homework in the top corner.

easy.def: A bright light in the night sky.
examples: I see a star.
Stars twinkle at night.
Make a wish on a star.

more.def: A huge ball of burning gas far away in space, which looks like a tiny light in the night sky.
examples: The sun is the closest star to Earth.
On a clear night, we counted hundreds of stars.
Some stars are much bigger than our sun.

easy.def: A shape with points.
examples: Draw a star.
The tree has a gold star.
She got a star on her paper.

more.def: A flat shape with five or more points.
examples: The flag has a white star in the corner.
The teacher put a gold star on my paper.
She cut a star out of yellow paper.

easy.def: A famous person.
examples: He is a movie star.
She is a singing star.
The star signed autographs.

more.def: A famous singer, actor or athlete.
examples: The singing star waved to the crowd.
He dreamed of becoming a famous movie star.
The soccer star signed shirts for the fans.

easy.def: To look at something for a long time.
examples: Do not stare.
The baby stared at me.
He stared at the sky.

more.def: To look at someone or something for a long time without looking away.
examples: The baby stared at the colorful toy.
We stared up at the stars.
It is not polite to stare at people.

easy.def: A spaceship in stories that travels to the stars.
examples: The starship flew past the moon.
I drew a starship.
The starship landed on a planet.

more.def: An imaginary spaceship in stories and movies that can travel far across space to other stars.
examples: The crew of the starship landed on a strange planet with purple trees.
I drew a picture of a starship with glowing blue engines.
In the book, the starship flew faster than light.

easy.def: To begin something.
examples: School starts at eight.
I start my book.
The race started.

more.def: To begin something, or to make something begin working.
examples: The concert starts at seven o'clock tonight.
Dad started the car and turned on the heat.
She started drawing as soon as she got the paper.

easy.def: The first part of something.
examples: It was a good start.
The start of the race is here.
We ate at the start.

more.def: The point at which something begins.
examples: The runners lined up at the start of the race.
We read the start of the story and wanted to hear more.
The first day of school is a fresh start.

easy.def: The first part of a meal.
examples: I had soup as a starter.
The starter was salad.
The starter was small.

more.def: A small dish that is served at the start of a meal.
examples: We had soup as a starter.
The starter was a small salad.
The waiter brought the starters.

easy.def: A player who begins a game.
examples: He is a starter on the team.
The starters ran on the field.
She is a starter.

more.def: A player who is chosen to play from the start of a game.
examples: The starters played the whole first half.
The starters ran onto the field.
The coach chose five starters.

easy.def: To make someone jump because of a sudden surprise.
examples: The noise startled me.
I did not mean to startle the cat.
The loud bang startled us.

more.def: To surprise someone suddenly so that they jump or are afraid for a moment.
examples: The loud noise startled me.
I did not mean to startle the cat when I walked in.
A sudden clap of thunder startled the children.

easy.def: To suffer from not having food.
examples: Animals starve in winter.
Plants starve without sun.
The stray cat was starved.

more.def: To suffer or die because there is not enough food.
examples: Some animals starve when snow covers the food.
The lost hikers were nearly starving.
We fed the stray cat so it would not starve.

easy.def: Very, very hungry.
examples: I am starving.
The starving puppy ate fast.
We were starving after the hike.

more.def: Suffering because you have not had enough food, or extremely hungry.
examples: I was starving after the long hike.
The starving puppy gulped down its food.
We are starving, so let's eat lunch.

easy.def: One of the parts of a country.
examples: Texas is a state.
I live in a state.
California is a big state.

more.def: One of the large regions that some countries, such as Mexico or Australia, are divided into.
examples: Alaska is the largest state in the United States.
Which state do you live in?
Each state has its own flag.

easy.def: The condition of something.
examples: The garden is in a good state.
My room is in a messy state.
Water in a frozen state is ice.

more.def: The condition that something is in at a certain time.
examples: Water can be in a solid, liquid or gas state.
The old house was in a poor state.
The park was in a clean state after the picnic.

easy.def: To say clearly.
examples: State your name.
Please state your answer.
He stated the rules.

more.def: To say something clearly in words.
examples: Please state your name and age.
The rules state that no one runs in the hall.
She stated her answer clearly.

related.def: To say something again, often in a new way.

easy.def: Something you say or write.
examples: She made a statement.
The statement is true.
Read the statement.

more.def: Words that say or tell something, spoken or written.
examples: The mayor made a statement about the storm.
Her statement was short and clear.
Read the statement on the card.

easy.def: A crackling noise on the radio.
examples: The radio has static.
I hear static.
The static is loud.

more.def: A crackling sound on a radio or TV caused by electricity in the air.
examples: There was static on the radio.
I heard static on the phone.
The static made it hard to hear the song.

easy.def: Not moving or changing.
examples: The picture is static.
A static pose.
The numbers are static.

more.def: Staying still or unchanged.
examples: The picture is static, not moving.
The numbers stayed static all year.
The scene was calm and static.

easy.def: A place where trains or buses stop.
examples: We waited at the train station.
The bus station is busy.
The station is near our house.

more.def: A place where trains or buses stop to let people on and off.
examples: We waited at the train station for Grandma.
The subway station was crowded.
The bus station is near the library.

easy.def: A place where TV or radio shows come from.
examples: My favorite radio station plays songs.
The TV station shows cartoons.
Turn to that station.

more.def: A company that sends out radio or TV programs.
examples: My favorite radio station plays music all day.
The TV station reported on the parade.
She listens to a news station on the way to school.

easy.def: A building where a group of workers does their job.
examples: The fire station is down the street.
Firefighters live at the station.
We toured the police station.

more.def: A building or place used for a special kind of work, such as fighting fires.
examples: The fire station is across from the school.
Scientists work at a weather station on the mountain.
The ranger station had maps of the park.

easy.def: A figure made of stone or metal.
examples: The statue stands in the park.
The statue is big.
I saw a statue of a horse.

more.def: A figure of a person or animal made from stone, metal or clay.
examples: A statue of a horse stands in the park.
The Statue of Liberty is a famous statue.
The artist carved a statue from marble.

easy.def: The state of something at a certain time.
examples: What is the status of the game?
The status is "open."
Check the status of the train.

more.def: The condition or situation of something at a particular time.
examples: The sign shows the status of the train, which is late.
She checked the status of her order online.
The doctor reported the status of the patient to the family.

easy.def: A person's place or rank in a group.
examples: He has the status of captain.
Her status as a champion was clear.
The king has high status.

more.def: A person's position or rank compared with others.
examples: He has the status of team captain.
In the old days, a person's status often depended on their family.
A gold medal gave her the status of a champion.

easy.def: A law.
examples: A statute is a law.
The statute says to stop at red lights.
The town has a statute.

more.def: A written law that has been made by a government.
examples: A town statute says that dogs must be kept on a leash in the park.
The new statute made it illegal to dump trash in the river.
The statute was passed by the state government.

easy.def: To be in the same place and not go.
examples: Stay here.
The dog stays home.
She stayed in bed.

more.def: To remain in a place and not leave.
examples: Please stay in your seats until the bell rings.
We stayed inside because of the thunder.
The turtle stayed under the rock all afternoon.

easy.def: To live somewhere for a little while.
examples: We stay at a hotel.
I stayed at Grandma's.
They stay for a week.

more.def: To live or sleep somewhere for a short time.
examples: We stayed at a cabin by the lake for the weekend.
My cousin is staying with us for a week.
The travelers stayed in a small hotel near the station.

easy.def: In a regular way.
examples: The rain fell steadily.
She worked steadily.
The line moved steadily.

more.def: In a way that is regular and does not stop or change.
examples: The rain fell steadily all night.
She worked steadily until she finished.
The line moved steadily forward.

easy.def: Not shaking or moving.
examples: Hold the ladder steady.
The boat is steady on the calm lake.
Use a steady hand to pour the milk.

more.def: Firm and not shaking; also, not changing much.
examples: She kept a steady hand while she painted the tiny flowers.
A steady rain fell all day.
He walked at a steady pace for miles.

easy.def: A thick, flat piece of meat or fish.
examples: Dad cooked a steak.
The steak is juicy.
We ate steak for dinner.

more.def: A thick, flat piece of meat or fish that is cooked and eaten.
examples: Dad grilled a steak for dinner.
The steak was cut into small pieces.
We had salmon steak and potatoes.

easy.def: To take what is not yours.
examples: The crow tried to steal my sandwich.
The squirrel steals seeds from the bird feeder.
The fox stole a hen in the story.

more.def: To take something that belongs to someone else without asking.
examples: The raccoon tried to steal food from the camp.
In the story, a thief stole the king's crown.
Squirrels sometimes steal seeds from the bird feeder.

related.def: Quiet and careful so no one sees or hears you.

easy.def: Moving quietly so nobody sees or hears you.
examples: The cat moved with stealth.
He walked with stealth.
She crept with stealth.

more.def: The act of moving or doing something quietly and secretly so that no one notices.
examples: The cat crept across the yard with great stealth, watching the bird.
The children moved with stealth so they would not wake the baby.
The fox used stealth to get close to the henhouse.

easy.def: Hot water that has turned to gas.
examples: Steam comes from the kettle.
The steam is hot.
A cloud of steam rose.

more.def: The cloud of hot gas that rises from boiling water.
examples: Steam rose from the hot soup.
The steam fogged up the mirror.
A cloud of steam came from the kettle.

easy.def: To cook food over boiling water.
examples: I steam the vegetables.
We steamed the rice.
She steamed the broccoli.

more.def: To cook food using the hot gas that rises from boiling water.
examples: Mom steamed the vegetables for dinner.
We steamed the dumplings in a basket.
The broccoli was steamed until soft.

easy.def: A very strong metal.
examples: The bridge is made of steel.
Steel is strong.
The knife is steel.

more.def: A very strong, hard metal made from iron, used to build many things.
examples: The tall building has a frame of steel.
Steel is used to make bridges.
The kitchen sink is made of steel.

easy.def: Going up or down very sharply.
examples: The hill is steep.
We climbed a steep path.
The stairs are steep.

more.def: Rising or falling at a sharp angle, so that it is hard to climb.
examples: The steep hill made us huff and puff on the way up.
We walked down the steep path very carefully.
The roof of the old barn is steep so that snow slides off.

easy.def: To soak something in water for a while.
examples: Steep the tea for a few minutes.
The leaves steep in hot water.
Let the beans steep overnight.

more.def: To let something soak in hot or cold water so that it becomes soft or gives its flavor to the water.
examples: Steep the tea bag in hot water for three minutes.
Mom let the dried beans steep overnight before she cooked them.
The herbs steeped in the pot and turned the water green.

easy.def: To make a vehicle go where you want.
examples: I steer the bike.
He steered the boat.
She steers the car.

more.def: To control the direction of a vehicle.
examples: I steered my bike around the puddle.
He steered the boat to the dock.
She steers the car with the wheel.

easy.def: The way that a vehicle is turned.
examples: The car has good steering.
The steering is tight.
The steering wheel is round.

more.def: The parts of a car, boat or bike that you use to turn it.
examples: The car has good steering and turns easily.
A broken steering wheel can be dangerous.
The boat's steering is controlled by a rudder.

easy.def: The long part of a plant that holds up the flower.
examples: The flower has a long stem.
The stem is green.
I picked the flower by its stem.

more.def: The main stalk of a plant that holds it up and carries water to the leaves and flowers.
examples: The flower has a long green stem.
I cut the stem of the rose.
Water moves up the stem to the leaves.

easy.def: To come from something.
examples: The problem stems from a mistake.
His fear stems from a fall.
The rule stemmed from an accident.

more.def: To come from or be caused by something.
examples: The problem stems from a small mistake.
His fear of dogs stems from a bite when he was little.
The rule stemmed from an accident last year.

easy.def: A very bad smell.
examples: The stench was awful.
A stench came from the trash.
I held my nose at the stench.

more.def: A very strong and unpleasant smell.
examples: The stench of rotten eggs filled the room.
We held our noses against the stench from the garbage.
A stench came from the old pond.

easy.def: One movement of your foot when you walk.
examples: Take one step forward.
The baby took a step.
I heard a step in the hall.

more.def: A single movement of the foot when you walk or run.
examples: The toddler took her first step.
With each step, the snow crunched under his boots.
He took three steps back to see the whole painting.

easy.def: A flat place to put your foot on stairs.
examples: Sit on the top step.
The steps are steep.
Do not trip on the step.

more.def: A flat surface in a set of stairs where you put your foot.
examples: Mind the last step because it is a little loose.
We sat on the front steps and ate ice cream.
She counted twelve steps up to the attic.

easy.def: One part of a job.
examples: The first step is to wash your hands.
Follow each step.
The recipe has four steps.

more.def: One part of a series of things you do to finish something.
examples: The first step in baking bread is mixing the dough.
Read each step before you begin the experiment.
The last step is to paint the model.

easy.def: To put your foot down and move.
examples: Step over the puddle.
Please step inside.
She stepped onto the bus.

more.def: To move by lifting a foot and putting it down somewhere.
examples: Step carefully over the slippery rocks.
He stepped aside to let the little girl pass.
Do not step on the sleeping cat.

easy.def: The man who is married to your mother but is not your father.
examples: My stepfather makes pancakes.
Her stepfather drives her to school.
I live with my mom and stepfather.

more.def: The man who has married your mother after your own father, and who becomes part of your family.
examples: My stepfather taught me how to ride a bike.
She baked a cake for her stepfather's birthday.
His stepfather came to cheer at every soccer game.

easy.def: The woman who is married to your father but is not your mom.
examples: My stepmother makes good pancakes.
Her stepmother is kind.
He lives with his stepmother.

more.def: The woman who is married to your father, when she is not the mother who gave birth to you.
examples: My stepmother taught me how to bake bread.
He gave his stepmother a card on her birthday.
In the old story, the girl's stepmother was kind in the end.

easy.def: A machine for playing music.
examples: I play music on the stereo.
The stereo is loud.
Turn off the stereo.

more.def: A machine with speakers that plays recorded music.
examples: I played my favorite song on the stereo.
The stereo is too loud.
Dad turned off the stereo.

easy.def: Strict and serious.
examples: The teacher gave a stern look.
His voice was stern.
A stern face.

more.def: Serious and strict in a way that is not very friendly.
examples: The teacher gave us a stern look.
Her stern warning made us listen.
The stern captain gave orders.

easy.def: The back of a ship.
examples: He stood at the stern.
The stern of the boat is back.
The sailor sat in the stern.

more.def: The back end of a ship or boat.
examples: He stood at the stern and watched the wake.
The captain steered from the stern.
The anchor hung off the stern.

easy.def: In a strict way.
examples: The teacher spoke sternly.
He looked sternly at us.
She sternly said no.

more.def: In a strict, serious way.
examples: The captain sternly ordered everyone below deck.
He looked at us sternly.
She sternly told the dog to stay.

easy.def: A thick soup of meat and vegetables.
examples: I ate beef stew.
The stew is hot.
Mom made stew.

more.def: A thick, hot meal made by cooking meat and vegetables slowly in liquid.
examples: We had beef stew for dinner.
The stew simmered on the stove.
Dad served the stew with bread.

easy.def: A woman who serves passengers on a plane.
examples: The stewardess gave us juice.
A stewardess helped us.
She is a stewardess.

more.def: A woman whose job is to look after passengers and serve them on a plane, ship or train; people now more often say flight attendant.
examples: The stewardess gave us juice and showed us how to buckle our belts.
A stewardess in a blue uniform greeted each passenger.
In old movies, the stewardess served meals on the plane.

easy.def: A thin piece of wood.
examples: The dog ran after the stick.

examples: We strolled through the park after dinner.
She strolled along the beach.
They strolled home in the sunshine.

easy.def: Having a lot of power.
examples: The strong man lifted the box.
An ox is strong.
The rope is strong.

more.def: Having great strength or power, and not easy to break.
examples: The strong wind blew down a branch.
She is strong enough to carry the heavy bag.
The bridge is built of strong steel.

easy.def: Easy to notice.
examples: There was a strong smell.
The tea is strong.
The sun is strong today.

more.def: Easy to notice, with a lot of flavor, smell or force.
examples: The strong smell of onions filled the kitchen.
The tea was too strong for me.
A strong wind blew across the field.

easy.def: In a powerful way.
examples: He pushed strongly.
I strongly believe it.
The wind blew strongly.

more.def: In a way that is powerful or firm.
examples: He pushed strongly on the door.
I strongly believe that you are right.
The wind blew strongly all day.

easy.def: Something that is built.
examples: The tower is a tall structure.
The bridge is a strong structure.
The structure is old.

more.def: Something that has been built, such as a building or a bridge.
examples: The Eiffel Tower is a tall structure.
The old bridge is a sturdy structure.
The bird built a neat structure out of twigs.

easy.def: The way the parts of something are put together.
examples: The structure of a leaf is thin.
The structure of the story was clear.
The body has a structure.

more.def: The way that the parts of something are arranged.
examples: The structure of a leaf helps it catch sunlight.
The story has a simple structure with three parts.
Scientists study the structure of the body.

easy.def: To try very hard to do something that is difficult.
examples: I struggle to lift the box.
She struggled to open the jar.
The ant struggled with the crumb.

more.def: To try hard to do something that is difficult or to get free.
examples: He struggled to carry all the bags.
The little bird struggled to get out of the net.
Some students struggle with math until they practice more.

easy.def: A hard try.
examples: It was a struggle to get up.
The long walk was a struggle.
Learning to read was a struggle.

more.def: A hard effort to do something difficult, or a long fight against a problem.
examples: Climbing the steep hill was a struggle.
It was a struggle to stay awake.
Their struggle for clean water lasted many years.

easy.def: To walk in a proud way.
examples: The rooster strutted.
She strutted down the hall.
The peacock struts.

more.def: To walk in a proud, showy way with your head held high.
examples: The rooster strutted across the yard as if he owned it.
She strutted down the hall in her new boots.
The peacock strutted and showed off its beautiful tail.

easy.def: A short piece that is left.
examples: I kept the ticket stub.
A pencil stub.
The stub is short.

more.def: A short piece that is left after the rest is used or torn off, like a pencil end or part of a ticket.
examples: I kept the ticket stub from the movie in my scrapbook.
The pencil was down to a short stub.
He tore off the stub and kept it as proof.

easy.def: To bump your toe hard on something.
examples: I stubbed my toe.
He stubbed his toe on the chair.
She stubbed her toe.

more.def: To hurt your toe by hitting it hard against something.
examples: I stubbed my toe on the leg of the table.
He stubbed his toe and hopped around the room.
Watch out so you do not stub your toe on the step.

easy.def: Short stalks left in a field after the crop is cut.
examples: The field was full of stubble.
Stubble is sharp.
The stubble pricked my feet.

more.def: The short stalks of a crop that are left standing in a field after harvest, or short, rough hair that grows on a man's face.
examples: After the wheat was cut, only stubble remained in the field.
The stubble was sharp and scratched my legs.
Dad has stubble on his chin when he forgets to shave.

easy.def: Not wanting to change your mind.
examples: The stubborn puppy would not come inside.
My stubborn dog will not take a bath.
Do not be stubborn. Try the peas.

more.def: Refusing to change your mind or do what others want.
examples: He was too stubborn to admit that he was lost.
The stubborn stain would not come out.
The stubborn mule refused to cross the bridge.

easy.def: A person who goes to school.
examples: The student reads a book.
Each student has a desk.
A new student joined our class.

more.def: A person who is learning at a school or college.
examples: Every student received a new notebook.
The student raised her hand.
The new student sat by the window.

easy.def: A room where an artist works.
examples: The painter has a studio.
The studio is full of paint.
She works in her studio.

more.def: A room or building where an artist, musician or photographer works, or where movies and shows are made.
examples: The artist painted in a bright studio with big windows.
The band recorded its songs in a music studio.
The photographer set up lights in her studio.

easy.def: To learn by reading and thinking.
examples: I study for my test.
She studies math.
We studied frogs.

more.def: To spend time learning about something by reading and thinking.
examples: I study my spelling words every night.
Scientists study the stars with telescopes.
She studied maps to plan the trip.

easy.def: Learning about something with care.
examples: The study of space is fun.
Scientists did a study of bees.
Her study took an hour.

more.def: A careful look at something to learn about it.
examples: The scientists published a study about bees.
A study of birds showed that many fly south.
Her study of the volcano took three years.

related.def: Spending a lot of time studying.

easy.def: Things that you do not name.
examples: I packed my stuff.
Put your stuff away.
There is stuff in the box.

more.def: Things or materials that are not named exactly.
examples: Put all your stuff in your backpack before you leave.
What is that sticky stuff on the table?
There is a lot of old stuff in the attic.

easy.def: Warm and without fresh air.
examples: The room is stuffy.
It is stuffy in here.
The stuffy attic is hot.

more.def: Without enough fresh air, so it feels close and warm.
examples: The room was stuffy, so we opened a window.
The attic was hot and stuffy in the summer.
I could not breathe in the stuffy car.

easy.def: Blocked, so you cannot breathe through your nose.
examples: I have a stuffy nose.
My nose is stuffy.
A cold gives me a stuffy nose.

more.def: Blocked up, so that it is hard to breathe through your nose.
examples: I have a stuffy nose because of my cold.
My nose got stuffy and I could not smell the soup.
A stuffy nose can make it hard to sleep.

easy.def: To trip and almost fall.
examples: I stumbled on a rock.
She stumbled over the toy.
He stumbled on the stairs.

more.def: To trip over something and nearly fall.
examples: I stumbled over a rock on the trail.
She stumbled on the stairs but caught the rail.
He stumbled in the dark.

easy.def: The part of a tree left in the ground.
examples: I sat on the stump.
The stump was wide.
A frog sat on the stump.

more.def: The part of a tree trunk that stays in the ground after the tree is cut down.
examples: We sat on a tree stump to eat our lunch.
A squirrel hid nuts under an old stump.
The stump showed rings that told how old the tree was.

easy.def: To ask something so hard that no one knows the answer.
examples: That riddle stumps me.
The question stumped the class.
It stumped everyone.

more.def: To puzzle someone so much that they cannot find the answer.
examples: That riddle really stumps me.
The hard question stumped the whole class.
The magic trick stumped everyone in the room.

easy.def: To surprise someone so much that they cannot speak.
examples: The news stunned us.
He was stunned.
The loud bang stunned me.

more.def: To shock or surprise someone so much that they cannot speak or move for a moment.
examples: The news stunned the whole class, and nobody said a word.
The sudden thunder stunned the dog.
I was stunned by the amazing magic trick.

easy.def: Very beautiful or amazing.
examples: The view was stunning.
She wore a stunning dress.
A stunning sunset.

more.def: Extremely beautiful, impressive or surprising.
examples: The view from the top of the mountain was stunning.
She wore a stunning blue dress to the dance.
We watched a stunning sunset over the ocean.

easy.def: A dangerous or tricky act.
examples: The stunt was amazing.
He did a stunt on his bike.
A stunt performer jumped.

more.def: A difficult or daring act that is done to show skill or to be exciting.
examples: The rider did a stunt on his bike.
A stunt performer jumped over the cars in the movie.
The circus had a stunt with a flying trapeze.

easy.def: Not showing good thinking.
examples: Leaving the door open was a stupid thing to do.
That was a stupid mistake.
I felt stupid when I forgot my own name.

more.def: Showing poor thinking or a lack of common sense.
examples: It was a stupid mistake to leave the gate open, and the sheep got out.
Running into the street without looking is a stupid thing to do.
He felt stupid after locking his keys inside the car.

easy.def: Being foolish or not using your brain.
examples: His stupidity was funny.
It was an act of stupidity.
Stupidity is not thinking.

more.def: The quality of being foolish or showing a lack of good thinking.
examples: His stupidity caused the mess.
It was an act of stupidity to run into the road.
I am sorry for my stupidity.

easy.def: Strong and well made.
examples: The chair is sturdy.
A sturdy boot.
A sturdy fence.

more.def: Strong and solid, so that it will not break easily.
examples: The sturdy table held all of the heavy books.
She wore sturdy boots for the muddy hike.
The old oak tree had a sturdy trunk.

easy.def: To repeat sounds when you talk.
examples: He stutters.
She stuttered a little.
He stuttered when he was nervous.

more.def: To repeat or stop on certain sounds when you speak, so the words do not come out smoothly.
examples: He stutters when he is nervous.
She stuttered on the first word of her speech.
Some people stutter, and it takes patience to listen.

easy.def: A way of doing something.
examples: I like her style.
He writes in a funny style.
The house has a modern style.

more.def: A particular way of doing, making or looking.
examples: I like her style of dressing.
The author writes in a funny style.
The house is built in an old-fashioned style.

easy.def: Looking neat and fashionable.
examples: She wore a stylish hat.
A stylish coat.
The shop is stylish.

more.def: Looking smart and fashionable, with a nice, up-to-date style.
examples: She wore a stylish red hat and matching gloves.
The stylish new shop sold bright coats and scarves.
He looked stylish in his new jacket.
